title: Non-pressure ulcer depth and burn extent
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the ulcer, or for the burn extent (T31) when the note is about a burn (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/24/2026
Reason for Admission: Extensive thermal burns

Vitals: BP 118/74, HR 88, SpO2 98% on room air

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive (Fatigue)
Integumentary: Positive (Burn)
Neurological: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Genitourinary: Negative

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 77-year-old female who presented to the emergency department following a kitchen fire. She sustained extensive flame burns.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for management of extensive thermal injuries. Physical examination revealed flame burns covering 35% of the body surface area. Of these injuries, 25% are classified as third degree (full thickness). The patient was stabilized with aggressive fluid resuscitation. Surgical intervention was performed to debride non-viable tissue. Given the extent of the full thickness injuries, grafting is planned and was initiated during the inpatient stay. The patient tolerated the procedures well and remained stable throughout the hospitalization.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Extensive flame burns
- Third degree burns

Discharge Medications:
- Morphine IR (as needed for pain)
- Cephalexin 500mg BID
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours

Follow-up: Follow up with Burn Unit clinic in 7 days for dressing change.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, MD, 05/24/2026
explanations: Burns of 30-39% of the body with 20-29% third degree: T31.32 (HCC 385).

distractors.why: 20-29% third degree is documented: the second character after the extent is 2.
